clue.text: A particular form of hatred

parts.note: taken as written
a version is one particular form of something

explanation.surface: Someone is describing a special kind of loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A particular form of' reads like a phrase introducing the definition, but it is all wordplay; only 'hatred' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or loathing, a near synonym of hatred.

clue.text: Talleyrand's inauguration divides a French town's representatives

indicators.note: something that divides splits another piece apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: Agen is a town in south-west France, plus S from the possessive

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so the first letter of the name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Talleyrand

explanation.surface: The French statesman Talleyrand's swearing-in splits a town's delegates.
explanation.walkthrough: Talleyrand was a French diplomat, so the French town fits the picture; his name only gives T, which goes between the town and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of others, so they are representatives.

clue.text: Complete before wrapping it up after noon

indicators.note: wrapping means going round, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An instruction to finish before tidying it all away in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete before' reads as finish first, but 'before' is ERE, which wraps the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, with nothing missing, so it is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Helping to make this implementation easy

indicators.note: helping to make something means being just a part of it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Advice on how to make a new procedure easy to carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple is straightforward and not difficult, which is what easy means.

clue.text: Some horse racing is honest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flat racing, run on ground without jumps

explanation.surface: A claim that a bit of horse racing is above board, which punters may doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat racing is held on level ground without fences; the phrase also means fair and genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means straightforward and trustworthy, while flat racing takes place on level turf.

clue.text: Fighting for part of London to embrace independence

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something in your arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
I is the standard abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A rallying cry about a London district fighting for its own independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who see action are in combat, so action is a noun for fighting.

clue.text: Disgrace of knight found with office worker in bed

indicators.note: being in something means being held inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
N is the chess notation for knight
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Scandal: a knight is discovered in bed with a temporary secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is the state of being despised or dishonoured, a sense close to disgrace.

clue.text: Bit of effort in restoration of print leads to identity of brave

indicators.note: restoring something rebuilds it, so the letters are put together in a new order
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of effort
letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the leads of a word are the letters at its front

parts.note: the first two letters of identity

explanation.surface: Effort put into restoring an old print reveals who a hero was.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid describes someone fearless and bold, so it means brave.

clue.text: One not disposed to pining — not any more

definitions.note: read cryptically as a person who is no longer, someone who does not long
definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: someone who does not long for things
second meaning: no more, at this point ceased

explanation.surface: A contented person who has stopped yearning for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: a longer is someone who longs, so a 'no longer' is someone who never pines.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means previously but not now, the same as not any more.

clue.text: Guess what? Finally, after a couple of escapes, I marry

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the first two letters of escapes

indicators.note: a couple means two, so just the opening pair of letters of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of what
taken as written
to mate is to pair up or marry

explanation.surface: A teasing 'Guess what?' before announcing that, after a few escapes, the speaker is finally getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guess what?' looks like a conversational opener, but 'Guess' alone is the definition; 'what' supplies only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make an approximate judgement, which is what a guess is.

clue.text: Drop in street — nothing seen around after one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something seen around another thing surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score
the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A traffic report: a dip in a street where nothing has been noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' sounds like a dip in the road, but it is the verb: to put in drop by drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is literally to introduce a liquid drop by drop, so the phrasal verb drop in fits.

clue.text: Right to stand by article about Brook's sensational story

indicators.note: standing by something means being placed right next to it
about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: the definite article
a rill is a small brook or stream
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A legal phrase about a right to stand by an article concerning someone called Brook.
explanation.walkthrough: The article wraps around the brook, and the R for right stands by at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a novel or film full of suspense and excitement, a sensational story.

clue.text: Humble pie ultimately eaten by fellow after debt is halved

indicators.note: halving a word throws away one of its two halves
after places the piece that follows it at the front, so the halved word comes first

parts.note: the first half of debt

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside whatever eats it

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of pie

explanation.surface: A man eats humble pie once half his debts are cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble pie' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Humble' is the definition, and 'pie' just gives its last letter, which sits inside MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, which is what humbling them does.

clue.text: Used expert to secure regular trade with Germany

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert
custom is the regular business of patrons
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A seasoned dealer secures steady business with Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The expert's letters split after the C so the regular trade sits inside. 'Used' is the adjective, as in used to the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used to something means habituated to it, which is what accustomed means.

clue.text: Aware of king following exercises to cure pet vice

indicators.note: following means coming after, fixing the order of the pieces

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: curing a vice reforms it, so its letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: R for Rex, Latin for king
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch, after his workouts, sets out to cure himself of a favourite bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone perceptive notices things readily, so they are aware and quick to see.

clue.text: Inclination for a writer to celebrate in song

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, something that writes
to chant is to sing or intone in celebration

explanation.surface: An author's natural urge to break into song in celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination for' reads as one phrase, but 'for' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or tendency, which is an inclination.

clue.text: Baffled for the most part about Rooney initially having time for a prostitute

indicators.note: having means holding alongside, so another piece is added on
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another
for the most part means mostly, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: stumped means baffled

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the name

parts.note: the first letter of Rooney
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A nod to the tabloid story of footballer Wayne Rooney paying for a call girl, leaving everyone puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Rooney is an England footballer whose dealings with prostitutes made headlines. Strumpet is an old word for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an archaic, contemptuous term for a prostitute or loose woman.

clue.text: Poison sent Arab reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about in confusion, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is poisoned and staggers about.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratsbane is an old name for rat poison, usually arsenic, so it is a type of poison.

clue.text: Fancy one more before going with us? It's immaterial

indicators.note: before fixes the order, putting one piece ahead of another

parts.note: extra means additional, more

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, inviting a decorative rearrangement of letters

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if we'd like one more drink before leaving with them, then shrugs that it doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy one more' reads as an offer of another drink; really 'Fancy' rearranges 'one' and 'more' gives EXTRA, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraneous is irrelevant to the matter in hand, which is one sense of immaterial.

clue.text: Charge account covers milk

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting on top, so one piece comes above the other

parts.note: ACC is a common abbreviation for account
to milk a situation is to exploit or use it

explanation.surface: A bill for the dairy delivery: the account pays for the milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' sounds like paying for something, but in this down clue it puts one piece on top of the other; 'milk' is the verb, to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with an offence is to accuse them formally.

clue.text: Raves about English composer

indicators.note: about can mean round and round, in a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A critic enthuses over an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Varèse was not English: 'English' only supplies a letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born American composer of experimental modern music.

clue.text: Make off hastily when Italian turns up during strike

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to beat is to strike

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means being read from bottom to top

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian worker arrives in the middle of a strike and quickly leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is an informal command or idiom meaning to go away quickly, to scram.

clue.text: Rector falls from horse in race

indicators.note: falling from something means coming off it, so that letter is lost

parts.note: a courser is a swift horse, a poetic word for a charger
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a tumble from his mount during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Courser is a literary word for a fast horse; removing the R leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A race can be a course, as in a watercourse or millrace, a channel along which water runs.

clue.text: It offers protection to society before rebel captures king

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is placed within another
before puts one piece ahead of what follows

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
taken as written
Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A political claim that something shields the public before a rebel seizes the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade, leader of the 1450 Kentish revolt, is the rebel crosswords most often use; the king goes in after his first letter.

clue.text: Surface of soft vegetable caught by artist from the east

indicators.note: something caught is held inside whatever catches it
in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
p is piano, the musical marking for soft
a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: An artist painting a soft vegetable, perhaps a squashy marrow, in an Eastern style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surface' looks like a noun, the outside of the vegetable, but here it is the verb: to come up into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to emerge or come into view, which is to appear.

clue.text: I'm taking a gamble grabbing Bordeaux's centre forward

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a punt is a bet or gamble

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of Bordeaux

clue.text: Rock drummer's back on ecstasy pursuing endless pretty girls

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the final letter is dropped
pursuing means coming after, fixing the order of pieces

parts.note: totty is British slang for attractive young women

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of drummer

explanation.surface: A rock drummer, high on ecstasy, chases an endless stream of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre beside 'drummer', but it is the verb: to sway unsteadily. Totty is dated British slang for attractive women.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to rock or sway unsteadily as if about to fall.

clue.text: Follower of a trend he created

indicators.note: something created is made anew, so these letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who follows a fashion that one man started.
